newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks to firm but market wary ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks to firm but market wary ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Tokyo stocks will likely firm on Tuesday, supported by investors' strong appetite for issues related to a recovery of the domestic economy, brokers said.

Investors are expected to remain cautious of export-oriented issues, as the Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting scheduled for later in the day may have an impact on the currency market, they added.
On Monday, the 225-share Nikkei average gained 165.02 points or 0.81 percent to close at 20,489.75. Its June futures rose 180 to 20,550.
"Investors' demand has been strong in issues driven by domestic demand, and this will firmly support the market," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
The market will also be encouraged by Monday's release of names of companies that will list their stock options on the Tokyo and Osaka exchanges in July, brokers said.
The companies include Sony Corp, Toyota Motor Corp and other blue-chip issues. This is likely to stimulate fresh buying momentum in the issues, they said.

But some said shares of exporters such as high-technology issues would be capped by the yen's recent strength and investors' cautious stance ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee later in the day.
Losing sectors were led by precision instruments, brokerages, ship building, banks, and automobiles.
DKB's shares fell 70 yen to stand at 1,400 yen at mid-session, making the bank the six largest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
"(The DKB news) sparked worries that bank shares might be hit by profit-taking after they had managed to recover recently," said a broker at a second-tier securities house.
Shares in Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) also fell, hurt by Monday's news of a possible cut in its credit ratings.
LTCB's shares lost 21 yen to stand at 366 at midday.
Earlier in the day, shares of companies that announced share buy-back plans surged, but they later shed part of their gains.
Nichimen Corp was 27 yen higher at 411, after having been bid-only. Mars Engineering Co Ltd was bid-only at 2,360 yen at 0200 GMT, against Monday's 2,200.

Issues, such as Sega Enterprises Ltd and Seven-Eleven Japan Co Ltd, which received approval to list stock options on the Tokyo and Osaka exchanges on July 18 rose initially, but the gains later fizzled.
By sector, the major gainers were rubber, electric power, fisheries, retailers, and land transport.
